sentences.text: His submission is placed on record.
3. Though the case is posted for admission, it is taken up for a final hearing with the consent of both counsel.
4. The learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance company has submitted that the accident took place on 16.10.2014, at the busiest place in front of Raghavendra lodge, Raichur.

The complainant-deceased filed complaint on 17.10.2014 at 1.00 p.m. and the complaint discloses that the deceased sustained injuries only to his left foot and toe, and no other parts of his body has sustained injuries.
The same was also admitted by PW.1 in her cross examination.
The claimants in collusion with the police and the owner of the car, have invented a false story about planting the said car with the sole object of claiming compensation.
Further it is submitted that it is a clear case of fraud and misrepresentation with a sole object of claiming compensation from insured vehicle which amounts to fraud and misrepresentation.

5. In this regard, the learned counsel for the appellant relied on the decision reported in Supreme Appeals Reporter (Civil) 2004 in a case of Ramachandra Singh Vs. Savitri Devi and others and on a decision of Apex court reported in (2012 I, Supreme court cases page 476 in a case of Union of India & others Vs. Ramesh Gandhi.

entities.text: Ramachandra Singh Vs. Savitri Devi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Union of India & others Vs. Ramesh Gandhi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the Insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.
Further it is submitted that the tribunal has also committed an error by overlooking Ex.P.1 in column No.6 where the name of the accused is shown as Jabu M Naik.
However, on subsequent investigation it was found that the driver did not hold a driving license.

As such,
concerned police without any basis in order to facilitate the claimants in getting compensation have planted a licensed driver showing Chandrashekhar @ Babu Nayak Mettappa Pawar @ Jabu.

entities.text: Chandrashekhar @ Babu Nayak Mettappa Pawar @ Jabu
entities.label: OTHER_PERSON

sentences.text: Further, it is submitted that the appellant had filed application under Order 11 Rule 14 R/w Section 151 CPC, calling upon the claimant's advocate to produced MLC case sheet of different hospitals to prove that there is nexus in the injuries and cause of death.
But the claimants have failed to furnish primary medical records at an undisputed point of time to establish the cause of death.
On all these grounds sought for allow this appeal.

6. As against this learned counsel for the respondent who has submitted that the tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record in para No.10 of the impugned judgment, the tribunal has assigned proper reasons to prove the case of the respondent, that there are no grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and award passed by the tribunal.
On all these ground sought for dismissal of this petition.

7. A perusal of para 10 of the judgment, the tribunal has observed as under:
10) On the basis of evidence on record, learned counsel for Respondent no.3 has filed his written arguments stating that petitioners have failed to prove the nexus between the injuries caused in the accident and death of deceased Chandappa.
He has relied on certain decisions on this aspect.

Principles stated in these cases is that where the petitioners have failed to prove the nexus between the injuries sustained in the accident and death of deceased they are not entitled to claim compensation.

In MFA The Branch Manager National Insurance vs Smt Huligemma And Ors on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28672885/
3 No.1572/08 (MV), our Hon'ble High Court has held that petitioner in that case died during the pendency of the petition and It was not proved that he died due to injuries sustained in the accident.

entities.text: MFA The Branch Manager National Insurance vs Smt Huligemma And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the Court hald that there is no nexus between the injuries and the death of injured claimant.

Similarly, in the decision reported in 2013 Kant M.A.C. 667 (Kant), our Hon'ble High Court has held that in absence of any nexus between nature of injuries sustained and cause of death of deceased, dismissed of claim petition justified.
In that case, deceased died due to Lung infection and not due to injuries sustained in accident.
Principles laid down in these cases are applicable depending on the evidence produced in the case.
In the present case, deceased Chandappa himself has given statement before the police on 17.10.2014 1.e., on the next day of accident.

On the basis of his statement, case was registered against respondent no.1 at that time he has stated that car run over his left foot and he sustained severe injuries on the left foot and he was admitted in Government hospital, Lingasugur.
Subsequently.
due to severe injuries, he was referred to Bagalkot hospital.
Therefore, there is delay in filing the complaint.
PME report of the deceased Chandappa is produced at Ex.P4 in which, the Medical Officer.
Government hospital, Lingasugur has clearly mentioned that death of the deceased is due to injuries sustained in the car accident.
Cause of death is stated as due to Hypoxia and shock due to hemorrhage due to head injury.
It is true that in his statement, the deceased has not stated that he has also sustained head injury in the accident.
It is necessary to observe that since from the date of accident l.e., on 16.10.2014 till his death deceased Chandappa was under medical treatment.

Firstly at Government hospital, Lingasugur and thereafter at Kerudi hospital, Bagalkot and again he was shifted to Government hospital,
Lingasugur and he died on 19.10.2014 in the Government hospital at Lingasugur I.e.,
4th day after the accident.
Petitioners had not produced any medical receipts and treatment certificates of Kerudi hospital.
Bagalkot.
Therefore, Respondent no.3 was disputing about treatment given to the deceased at Kerudi hospital, Bagalkot.

Subsequently, petitioners have produced Ex.P9 & 10 documents, which go to support the case of petitioners that deceased Chandappa was admitted in Kerudi hospital,
Bagalkot and Ex.P9 Cash Memo issued by the said hospital towards admission fees.
Similarly.
Ex.P10 CT Scan Brain (PLAIN) issued by Kerudi hospital, Bagalkot.
Name of the patient is shown as Chandappa Doddamant and he was subjected to CT Scan Brain (Plain).
Opinion is multiple acute focal infarcts in bilateral superior frontal lobes.
On 18.10.2014, the deceased was referred back to CMO..

Government hospital,
Lingasugur from Kerudi hospital.
Copy of the letter is produced by the petitioners.
It is also stated that patient was having head injury risk of transportation was also informed to the patient as mentioned in this letter.
All the reports of Kerudi hospital were also sent to CMO, Government hospital, Lingasugur.
On the next day 1.c., on 19.10.2014 deceased died at Government hospital, Lingasugur.
Therefore, there is sufficient material on record to prove the nexus between the injuries sustained by the deceased Chandappa in the accident and his death.

It is also necessary to refer to the contents of The Branch Manager National Insurance vs Smt Huligemma And Ors on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28672885/
4 charge sheet filed by the police as per Ex.P6.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the charge sheet, it is clearly mentioned that respondent no.1 dashed the car to deceased Chandappa and he fell down and sustained Injury on the back of his head.
Therefore observation of the Kerudi hospital that deceased had sustained head injury has to be held that it was caused in the motor vehicle accident and he died due to said injury.

Therefore, contention of the respondent no.3 that there is no nexus between the injuries sustained by the deceased in the accident and his death cannot be accepted.
11) Respondent no.3 has also disputed that respondent no.1 was not having valid and effective driving licence to drive the car.
Petitioners have produced the D.L. Extract of respondent no.1 at Ex.P7.
Name of the respondent is shown as Chandrashekar.
In the charge sheet, the police have shown his name as Chandrashekhar @ Jabu Nayaka S/o Metapopa Pawar Jabu.

Moreover,
respondent no.3 has not challenged the charge sheet against respondent no.1 nor respondent no. 1 has challenged the same.
Therefore, respondent no.3 has also failed to prove that respondent no.1 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the car at the time of accident.
Under these circumstances, I hold that petitioners have proved this Issue.
"affirmative".
Accordingly.

I answer this Issue in the "affirmative"
8.

A perusal of the papers placed before the Tribunal makes it crystal clear that on the basis of a complaint filed by one Chandappa, Lingasugur police have registered the case against accused-Jabu Nayaka, the driver of the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-36/434 for the offences punishable under Section 279, 338 of IPC and Section 187 of M.V.Act and submitted the FIR to the Court on 17.10.2014.
In the FIR itself in column No.3(c), the delay in filing the FIR has clearly stated that since the complainant has admitted to the Hospital, he could not file his complaint in time.
Thereafter, police have visited the spot, drawn the spot mahazar/Ex.P2 and prepared a rough sketch.
During the course of treatment, the complainant succumbed to the accidental injuries.

The inquest panchanama has also been conducted as per Ex.P3, in para-11 of the inquest panchanama,
the Investigating Officer has narrated the reasons for the death of the deceased.
The post mortem report/Ex.P4 reveals the cause of death that the deceased died due to hypoxia and shock due to an intracranial hemorrhage due to head injury.

9. After obtaining the post mortem report and the statement of witnesses, the Investigating Officer has submitted the charge-sheet against the driver of the vehicle i.e. car bearing Reg.No.KA-36/N-0434 against Jabu Nayaka @ Chandrashekhar, for the commission of offence punishable under Sections 279, 304-A of IPC and Section 187 of M.V.Act.
- 10 - 10.
During the course of cross-examination, RW.1 has clearly admitted that they have not conducted investigation in this case.

Without placing any legal evidence before the Tribunal, RW.1 has stated in his evidence that in the FIR the name of accused is shown as Jabu Nayaka and subsequently, at the time of filing charge-sheet, the name of Jabu Nayak @ Chandrashekhar, the driver name is mentioned, this cannot be accepted.

sentences.text: Considering the oral and documentary evidence placed before the Tribunal, the Tribunal has rightly and properly appreciated the evidence on record and given finding that there are no legal grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal filed by the appellant/insurance company is dismissed.
- 11 - (ii) The amount deposited before this Court, if any, by the appellant/insurance company shall be transmitted to the concerned Tribunal.
